Hi Rachel / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. AtlasHealth is ready to move into a short hands-on POC focused on: prompt refinement for clinical summaries, routing logic for multi-model fallbacks, and a short load test to validate token budgets. Can we book a two-part cadence: (1) 90-minute technical kickoff + prompt review with our engineering and clinical SME, (2) 2-hour hands-on workshop for routing/load tests? Ideally in the week of May 3 or May 10 (PST).

A few constraints on our side: we prefer hosted trial initially, but we need to verify whether quota bumps for a short load test are feasible. Also want to confirm request/response latency targets (sub-300ms for small summaries) and a token budget cap during the trial.

Attached is our internal outline (Atlas_POC_Scope_v2.pdf).

Look forward to proposed times.

—Maya

Adding a quick technical note from infra/ops perspective.

If you start on Hosted: we can provide a temporary quota bump for a focused load test up to ~120 req/s with burst handling, for a 4-hour window. That typically covers token budgets up to ~1.5M tokens per hour depending on model choice. If Atlas needs more sustained throughput or tight latency SLAs during the test, Dedicated trial nodes are the way to go — we can spin a small dedicated pool (2×A100 equivalent) for the week.

A couple of practicals for the load test:
- We need anonymized payload sizes + expected concurrency pattern (spikes vs steady).
- We'll run a dry-run at low scale first (15–30 minutes) to validate caching behavior and KV warmup.
- Please confirm test windows and a contact for run-day troubleshooting (Slack contact preferred).

Happy to join the hands-on workshop and help tune the batching/quantization hints.

—Ben

Thanks — quick operational checklist from infra/quotas:

1) Quota bump process (Hosted): we need a signed mutual action plan and an explicit start/end window. Lead time is ~48 hours to apply on our side. For the 4-hour load test Ben mentioned, share the desired start time and total token cap.
2) Token budget recommendation (starter): for routing + prompt refinement workload, we recommend starting with a 500k token cap/day during the trial, with an extra 1M token buffer for the scheduled load test.
3) Rate limits: we can temporarily raise per-minute request limits for the load window; concurrent request ceilings still enforced per-tenant, so plan to run distributed workers or staggered clients.
4) Dedicated option: provisioning takes ~3 business days for trial pool (we can pre-authorize if you need Dedicated for the week of May 10).

Please send the anonymized payload samples and preferred test window (UTC offset) so we can lock this in.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Product Operations, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
